findings.summary: Two statements about the B16 wall_clock check are wrong. They are the rule comment of WALL_CLOCK_TOLERANCE_S (scripts/traffic_log.py:75-76) and row 16 of docs/ODCHYLKY_V5.sk.md. Both say honest logs differ by less than 2 ms, and that only a step of the wall clock moves the difference. I measured all 103 H2 log pairs and every field pair that wall_clock binds. Honest differences reach 5.064 ms, and no clock step caused them. scripts/host_traffic.py reads the two clocks in two separate calls, so a thread switch between the reads moves the difference, and this grows with load. The 1 s bound is still about 200 times larger than every honest value, so no honest pair is refused. Only the stated number and its stated cause are wrong.

findings.summary: scripts/tests/test_traffic_stream_b18.py claims more than it checks, though the code itself meets the claims. Its module docstring (line 10) says no reader reads the request log whole. test_no_reader_reads_the_request_log_whole refuses only Path.read_bytes, Path.read_text and traffic_log.read_jsonl, so a reader using open(...).read() or readlines() would pass. Its comparison is json.dumps(..., default=repr) text (line 37), which cannot tell a tuple from a list or an int dict key from its string. My grep found no reader that reads the whole request log, and my type-aware comparisons found no difference, so no code fault hides behind this.
findings.evidence: grep of '.read()|readlines|read_bytes|read_text|splitlines' in scripts/traffic_log.py, collection_logs.py and lab_trial.py, and in campaign_report.load_traffic: none applies to the request log (the only whole read left is collection.warmup_failures, during capture, bounded by the warmup). My strict comparator (praca/skripty/fz_common.py diff: types, key order and key types, NaN-aware) gave 0 differences on 72,108 + 30,120 + 20,021 + 550 comparisons and on the 927 real-log items.
findings.suggested_fix: Also refuse builtins.open/io.open read()/readlines() of the request log path in that test, and compare with a type-aware comparison (or repr/pickle) instead of JSON text. Alternatively, narrow the docstring to what is checked.

traffic_stop. collection.py sends SIGUSR2, then stop_child(traffic, TRAFFIC_STOP_GRACE_S): killpg SIGTERM, wait 30 s, then SIGKILL, and the same in the finally block (an AST test checks both). host_traffic queues signals (SIGUSR2=12 before SIGTERM=15), sends no request after stop, and in-flight requests time out at TIMEOUT_S=10, so an honest end lies within about 10 s of post. The real self-test's clean session ends 0.5 s after post (3602.0 → 3602.5). lab_trial is not audited. A consistent move inside the grace can still change the order share, but only through user sessions that started D_max−30..D_max before the stop and lasted longer than that. On run 27, 116 of 105,070 measure sessions last >212 s, and ordering sessions exceed 242 s at 0.00077 (16/20,839; run 17: 5/6,706), which fits D_max's design level 0.001. The expected effect is about one session in 10^5, far below the tolerance.
